findings.problem: MetricWorkflow has no typestate enum; status and boolean flags allow illegal state combinations like status='new' with is_validated=true and is_sent=true simultaneously, and mark_sent bypasses validation entirely.
findings.failure_mode: Any caller can construct MetricWorkflow with contradictory fields or advance directly to 'sent' without validation, violating the domain lifecycle invariant that sent requires validated.
findings.fix: Replace status, is_validated, and is_sent with a single typestate enum like enum WorkflowState { Pending, Validated, Sent { sent_at_epoch_ms: u64 } } with a single field; make all constructors fallible and enforce transitions.

findings.problem: status is pub String instead of an enum. Any arbitrary string value ("sent", "DELETED", "", null-bytes) is valid, and mark_sent writes a magic string literal.
findings.failure_mode: Callers can set status to any string, including values the domain does not recognize; string comparison is fragile and the lifecycle state is not enforced by the type system.
findings.fix: Replace with a non-exhaustive enum: enum Status { Pending, Validated, Sent }. Remove is_sent and is_validated booleans entirely—they are subsumed by the enum variant.

findings.problem: is_validated: bool and is_sent: bool encode lifecycle state as independent booleans. There are 4 boolean combinations but only 2-3 valid lifecycle states (pending, validated, sent). The boolean encoding makes invalid states representable.
findings.failure_mode: (valid=false, sent=false), (valid=true, sent=false), (valid=true, sent=true), and (valid=false, sent=true) are all representable; the last is logically impossible, and the first two cannot distinguish 'never validated' from 'not yet sent'.
findings.fix: Replace both booleans with a single typestate enum that encodes the lifecycle as mutually exclusive variants, e.g. enum State { Pending, Validated, Sent { sent_at_epoch_ms: u64 } }.

findings.problem: sent_at_epoch_ms: Option<u64> is a separate field from is_sent: bool. The Option allows sent_at_epoch_ms=Some(t) while is_sent=false, or sent_at_epoch_ms=None while is_sent=true—both are invalid state combinations.
findings.failure_mode: The Option field can drift out of sync with the is_sent boolean, producing unreachable states that violate the invariant that sent_at_epoch_ms is present if and only if the workflow is sent.
findings.fix: Tuck sent_at_epoch_ms inside the typestate enum variant that owns it: State::Sent { sent_at_epoch_ms: u64 }. This makes the presence of the timestamp part of the type, eliminating the Option entirely.

findings.problem: id is pub String with no validation, no newtype wrapper, and no domain semantics. Any empty string, null bytes, or arbitrary-length string is accepted as a valid metric ID.
findings.failure_mode: Callers can construct MetricWorkflow with id="", id="  ", or an unbounded-length string that may exceed storage or indexing limits downstream. No domain invariant on id format or length is enforced at the type level.
findings.fix: Introduce a newtype: pub struct MetricId(String) or better pub struct MetricId(NonZeroU64) if IDs are numeric. Provide a fallible smart constructor that validates format/length and returns a typed error.

findings.problem: MetricWorkflow is constructed directly with raw primitives (String, String, bool, bool, Option<u64>). There is no parse boundary—no smart constructor, no fallible factory, no validation at the module boundary—so callers can construct any invalid domain state directly.
findings.failure_mode: The type exposes its internal representation as a public struct with public fields; callers bypass any lifecycle invariants, status constraints, and timestamp consistency rules by writing struct literals with arbitrary values.
findings.fix: Make all fields private (or remove the struct entirely in favor of an enum). Provide a single fallible constructor like fn try_new(id: impl Into<String>) -> Result<MetricWorkflow, NewError> that returns a valid-by-construction type. The type should be represented as an enum typestate, not a struct of primitives.

findings.problem: All fields of MetricWorkflow are pub, exposing the internal representation. This breaks encapsulation and allows callers to mutate status, booleans, and Option independently of any domain logic.
findings.failure_mode: External code can do item.status = ""; item.is_validated = false; item.is_sent = false; item.sent_at_epoch_ms = Some(0); without any domain logic or invariant enforcement, producing a struct that violates every domain rule.
findings.fix: Make all fields private or replace the struct with an enum typestate. Provide domain methods (e.g. validate(), mark_sent()) that enforce invariants at call sites.

findings.problem: mark_sent unconditionally sets status and is_sent without checking is_validated or any precondition. The lifecycle transition from validated to sent is not enforced.
findings.failure_mode: A MetricWorkflow in any state—including one with is_validated=false—can be marked as sent, violating the domain invariant that only validated metrics may be sent.
findings.fix: Replace mark_sent with a method on the typestate enum that is only callable from the Validated variant: fn mark_sent(self) -> MetricWorkflow. The type system enforces the precondition.

missing_evidence: no benchmark exists for mark_sent or MetricWorkflow construction
no profiler data for the hot path containing MetricWorkflow operations
no allocation analysis for String::to_string() and Vec allocations in mark_sent
no second-ring evidence (CI, sanitizer, or fuzz) for the typestate invariants
no command evidence that cargo fmt/check/clippy/test pass on this crate
residual_risk: Struct is entirely built on raw primitives with public fields, no typestate enum, no parse boundary, and a state-agnostic mutation function. Every Holzman law around make-illegal-states-unrepresentable, status-as-enum, bool-as-typestate, and parse-boundary is violated. Static review only; no commands executed. The crate must be redesigned with an enum typestate before any delivery.
